facts.text: In scope: where each operator came from, which server version introduced or changed it, what the pairing means semantically, how it is implemented, and how its documented guidance has shifted over time.

**C12. Until MongoDB 3.6, `$geoWithin` with `$centerSphere` matched only GeoJSON `Point` documents, not other GeoJSON geometry types.** SERVER-27968, "$geoWithin with $centerSphere does not find GeoJSON documents other than Points," was created 2017-02-09 against 3.4.0, classified Major (P3) under the Geo and Querying components, and fixed in 3.6.0-rc0. From 3.6 onward, `$geoWithin` + `$centerSphere` also matches GeoJSON `LineString` and `Polygon` documents. This is the single most consequential behavioral change to the pairing after its 2.4 creation.

An S2 cap is a region defined by *angular* distance from a centre, measured along the sphere's surface.** A cap of π/2 is a hemisphere; a cap of 180° or more contains the entire unit sphere; a negative radius yields an empty cap. 1. The radius argument is in **radians**, not metres, kilometres, miles, or degrees. This is stated in the operator reference itself and is the operator's single largest footgun, because passing a metre value produces a syntactically valid query. <https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/centerSphere/>

17. Historical defect worth knowing when reading old reports or running old servers: SERVER-27968, "`$geoWithin` with `$centerSphere` does not find GeoJSON documents other than Points." **S5. Unit conversion is the caller's responsibility and is not validated.** The server receives a bare number; `10 / 6378.1` is a 10 km radius only because the application chose that divisor. [M6, M7, H C4, E1, P4] — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/geospatial/2d/calculate-distances/

**S12. The radius must be a number and must satisfy `>= 0`, else the parse fails with "Radius must be a non-negative number".** The check is written `if (!radiusElt.isNumber() || !(radiusElt.number() >= 0))` — the `!(x >= 0)` form, which also catches `NaN` because every `NaN` comparison is false. [M13, H C8, E3] — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/geo/geoparser.cpp

**S21. `2dsphere` indexes are always sparse.** The `sparse` option is ignored; documents missing the indexed field (or holding `null` / an empty array there) get no index entry, so an index-backed `$geoWithin` never sees them. [M24] — single-pass claim, mechanism only. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/geospatial/2dsphere/

The two positions are compatible in substance — M and E infer from primary artifacts what P declines to assert without a MongoDB statement — but they are recorded separately because the confidence levels genuinely differ. Resolving this needs an experiment, not another search [E D4].
**Saturated on documented mechanism. Not saturated on empirical behaviour — and further search will not close the gap.**

**Magnitude estimates disagree across passes and should not be averaged:** M states ≈0.11%, ≈11 m on a nominal 10 km radius; H states ≈0.1%, ≈7 km at the equator, ≈200 m on a 200 km query; P states ≈0.1%, ≈10 m on 10 km. These are consistent in order of magnitude and differ in framing.

**A separate and larger accuracy bound** comes from the edge-cases pass [E19]: WGS84 equatorial radius is 6,378.137 km, polar 6,356.7523 km, mean (R1) 6,371.0087714 km — equatorial exceeds polar by about 0.34%. E infers that dividing by the equatorial radius understates the cap at high latitude by up to a few tenths of a percent (≈ tens of metres on a 10 km cap, ≈1.7 km on a 500 km cap), and that documents within ~0.3% of the boundary are not reliably classified **under any constant**. — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earth_radius

This report covers only the `$geoWithin` query operator when its shape argument is `$centerSphere` — a spherical cap defined by `[[<x>, <y>], <radius in radians>]`. It records boundary conditions (radius extremes, coordinate bounds, index-type boundaries), failure modes (silent wrong results, crashes, unit errors), and points where sources disagree.

16. `$geoWithin` returns **unsorted** results, which is why it is cheaper than `$near`/ `$nearSphere`; it carries no distance in the output and accepts no `$maxDistance`/ `$minDistance`. Ranking or "nearest N" semantics cannot be recovered from a `$centerSphere` predicate alone. <https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/geoWithin/>

Out of scope and deliberately not researched: `$near` / `$nearSphere`, `$geoIntersects`, the `$geoNear` aggregation stage, the `2d` and `2dsphere` index types as topics in their own right, GeoJSON as a format in its own right, and the sibling shape operators `$box`, `$center`, and `$polygon`. Those are separate frontier items. They appear here only where a claim about `$geoWithin` or `$centerSphere` cannot be stated without them.

**D2. Is bare `$within` still accepted by a current server?** The 2.4 manual deprecated it (https://mongoing.com/docs/reference/operator/query/geoWithin.html) and the current manual does not mention it at all (https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/geowithin/). This report covers only the internal mechanism of `$geoWithin` and of the `$centerSphere` shape that is passed to it: the containment predicate, the spherical-cap representation, the radian radius contract, index interaction, and the documented and code-level limits. Sibling operators (`$near`, `$nearSphere`, `$geoIntersects`, `$geoNear`), the other `$geoWithin` shapes (`$box`, `$polygon`, `$center`), and the wider geospatial-index domain are out of scope except where a claim about `$geoWithin`/`$centerSphere` cannot be stated without naming them.

18. `$geoWithin` "does not require a geospatial index", but an index improves performance. The same statement is made for `$centerSphere`: applications can use it without a geospatial index, though "geospatial indexes support much faster queries than the unindexed equivalents". — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/geoWithin/ and https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/centerSphere/ 19. The operator reference pages state that **both** `2dsphere` and `2d` indexes support `$geoWithin` and `$centerSphere`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/referen

11. `$near` is a match-execution operator and is not permitted in aggregation pipelines, so it cannot appear in a `$match` stage. `$geoWithin` carries no such restriction, which makes `$centerSphere` the practical way to express a radius filter mid-pipeline without reaching for `$geoNear` as the first stage. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/near/

**S11. `$geoWithin` carries no distance in its output and accepts no `$maxDistance`/`$minDistance` — ranking cannot be recovered from a `$centerSphere` predicate alone.** [E16] — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/geoWithin/

**S23. Before MongoDB 3.6, `$geoWithin` + `$centerSphere` matched only GeoJSON `Point` documents.** SERVER-27968, created 2017-02-09 against 3.4.0, Major/P3 under Geo and Querying: a 500 km cap returned no `Polygon` documents while an equivalent `$geometry` polygon query over the same data did. Fixed in 3.6.0-rc0. On any pre-3.6 server `$centerSphere` is a points-only predicate, and the failure mode is empty results, not an error. This is the most consequential behavioural change to the pairing since its creation. All four passes found it independently. [M28, H C12, E15, P17] — https://jira.mo

20. A dated engineering report (Artsy, 2023-02-10) documents the concrete consequence of choosing the wrong shape operator: with the planar `$center` and a degrees-per-km divisor (`25 / 111.32`), "edge cases near the top or bottom of the circle were likely to be evaluated correctly, while edge cases at the left and right were being incorrectly omitted" — a Santa Monica gallery was excluded from a 25 km Los Angeles radius. The fix was `$centerSphere` with `25 / 6378.1`. The east–west-only error pattern is the signature to look for when diagnosing a suspected `$centerSphere` problem that is real

**C2. `$geoWithin` was introduced in MongoDB 2.4 as the replacement for `$within`, which 2.4 deprecated.** The 3.4 manual states the version note verbatim: "`$geoWithin` replaces `$within` which is deprecated." MongoDB 2.4 was released 2013-03-19 and shipped enhanced geospatial support as a headline feature, including the `2dsphere` index and GeoJSON. Sources: https://mongoing.com/docs/reference/operator/query/geoWithin.html and https://docs.huihoo.com/mongodb/3.4/release-notes/2.4/index.html

**C9. `$geoWithin` is dispatched through a dedicated parser keyword in the matcher.** The server's query operator map contains `{"geoWithin", PathAcceptingKeyword::GEO_WITHIN}` and `{"geoIntersects", PathAcceptingKeyword::GEO_INTERSECTS}`, with `$near` / `$nearSphere` routed to `GEO_NEAR` and explicitly disallowed in contexts that cannot sort.

3. **A negative or NaN radius is rejected, not tolerated.** The server validates `radiusElt.number() >= 0` and raises `"Radius must be a non-negative number: "`. Note the predicate is written as `!(x >= 0)`, which is the form that also catches NaN — `NaN >= 0` is false, so NaN takes the error path. <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/geo/geoparser.cpp>
